source.title: DeepSeq: high-throughput single-cell RNA sequencing data labeling via web search-augmented agentic generative AI foundation models
source.citation: S. A. Al Dajani et al., 2025
source.authors: S. A. Al Dajani; Abel Sanchez; John R. Williams

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream cell-labeling performance across language models and reports how that performance changes with model scale, using task accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure language-model pretraining loss, sweep training tokens or compute, or fit scaling laws. Its reported comparisons of downstream labeling accuracy across models bear on V6. The exponential growth of single-cell datasets and future scaling projections are background or projections, not model-training results.
record.test_reason: The study compares off-the-shelf LLMs of different sizes (LLaMA3-1B, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o) on one downstream task, single-cell cell-type labeling. It plots parameter count against accuracy (Fig. 5). This is a weak, new-setting test of V6 only. Scale is confounded with model family, retrieval and closed models whose sizes are undisclosed. No loss, sweep or fit is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that agentic GPT-4o with retrieval reaches 82.5% labeling accuracy and beats static or smaller models. They say accuracy did not scale linearly with size, with diminishing returns without more domain-specific data. They assert that language-model scaling laws extend to biological annotation. That last claim is asserted rather than shown by a fit.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures downstream cell-labeling accuracy across model configurations; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss, sweep parameters/tokens/compute, fit power laws, or find compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Inference context differs: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o use agentic web search, whereas the local LLaMA model does not. The authors also state that returns diminish without more domain-specific single-cell data.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025 (as stated in the paper text)
record.problems: The evidence is for a single downstream biological annotation task, not pretraining loss or a controlled scaling sweep. Exact accuracy values are not provided for most model comparisons, and model size is confounded with inference context, including web search.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or parameter, token or compute sweep.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law test in another modality or regime. The single-cell growth curve (Fig. 1) concerns dataset sizes, not model training.
No relation to pretraining loss. No controlled model family, so predictability across scale cannot be established.

missing.what: Per-model labeling accuracies and parameter counts plotted in Figures 4 and 5. Only GPT-4o's 82.5% is stated in the text, so rows r2 to r4 lack values.

record.verdict_notes: This is weak evidence. There are 3 or so models from different families, closed models with undisclosed sizes, a 1.8T figure for GPT-4o without a source, and retrieval confounded with scale. Methods and Discussion disagree on whether GPT-3.5 used web search. 'Diminishing returns' on a log axis with few points is not a challenge to a power-law trend. The verdicts should be weighted lightly.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or parameter, token, or compute scaling sweep.
No scaling-law fits or tests of predictions from small runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or fitted parameter/token allocation trend.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The paper applies language models to biological annotation, but does not test whether a power-law form holds for other modalities or training regimes.
Tests cell-labeling accuracy across model configurations, but does not relate it to pretraining loss or establish quantitative predictability across scales.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of fitting choices and resulting curves.

rows.subject: gpt-4o
rows.operation_detail: Compared cluster-level predicted cell-type labels with manually curated ground truth.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the highest accuracy among the evaluated LLMs.
rows.check: A single model's accuracy (82.5%) is not a scaling comparison. The 1.8T parameter count for GPT-4o is an unofficial figure the paper asserts without a source.

rows.subject: GPT-3.5-turbo
rows.operation_detail: Compared cell-labeling accuracy with the LLaMA3-2-1B result.
rows.measure: Relative change in labeling accuracy across model comparisons
rows.baseline: LLaMA3-2-1B; its accuracy is not stated
rows.value: The accuracy leap from LLaMA3-2-1B to GPT-3.5-turbo was larger than the improvement from GPT-3.5-turbo to GPT-4o.
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative; the paper gives no accuracy value for GPT-3.5-turbo here. The paper also describes GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o as using agentic web search, unlike the local LLaMA model.
rows.check: This is the 1B-to-GPT-3.5 gain, which the paper calls a large 'leap'. The row should read as improvement with scale (observed), not partial. No accuracy values are given. The web-search confound is inconsistent in the text: Methods say only GPT-4o uses web search, while the Discussion says both GPT models do.

rows.subject: gpt-4o
rows.measure: Relative change in labeling accuracy across model comparisons
rows.baseline: GPT-3.5-turbo; its accuracy is not stated
rows.value: The improvement from GPT-3.5-turbo to GPT-4o was smaller than the leap from LLaMA3-2-1B to GPT-3.5-turbo, despite GPT-4o having significantly more parameters.
rows.note: This is a qualitative comparison; no per-model accuracy values for the comparison are stated.
rows.check: Smaller gain from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o. The direction is still upward but much weaker per added scale. No numbers are given, and GPT-3.5's parameter count is not stated.

rows.subject: Foundation models compared in Figure 5 (individual model set not specified in this statement)
rows.size_stated: Diminishing returns beyond 100B parameters are stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared model scale with cell-labeling accuracy.

conditions.value: cell-type labeling from top marker genes per cluster
the paper says diminishing returns occur without more domain-specific single-cell data

rows.measure: Relationship between model scale and labeling accuracy
rows.value: The paper describes diminishing returns beyond 100B parameters without more domain-specific single-cell data.
rows.note: This is the caption's qualitative summary of the comparison; no exact values for the plotted models are stated in the text.
rows.check: The Figure 5 caption states diminishing returns beyond 100B parameters. The plotted values and model set are not in the text. The caption also says active parameter counts are 'similar', which undercuts the scale axis.

rows.subject: LLaMA3-1B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated cell-labeling accuracy using marker-gene prompts.

conditions.value: local model; no agentic web search

rows.value: The paper says local LLaMA3-1B performed competitively given its size.
rows.note: The text elsewhere refers to LLaMA3-2-1B in its comparison with GPT-3.5-turbo; no exact accuracy for either naming is given here.
rows.check: 'Competitive given their size' is a qualitative remark with no value or comparison that shows a scaling trend.

relationships.condition: LLaMA3-1B (local) vs GPT-3.5-turbo on cell-type labeling
relationships.reason: r2: accuracy rises sharply from the 1B model to GPT-3.5. This is confounded with model family and possibly retrieval, and no values are given.
relationships.display_finding: GPT-3.5-turbo achieved sharply higher accuracy than LLaMA3-1B, with model family and possibly retrieval confounding the comparison.

relationships.condition: GPT-3.5-turbo vs GPT-4o, and models beyond ~100B parameters
relationships.reason: r3 and r4: gains shrink markedly at larger scale, which the authors call diminishing returns. The evidence is qualitative, the sizes are unofficial, and family and retrieval are confounded.
relationships.display_finding: Gains shrank markedly beyond roughly 100B parameters, although size estimates were unofficial and model family and retrieval varied together.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Compared model configurations on single-cell RNA-seq cell-type labeling
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports accuracy gains across some model comparisons but says the gain from GPT-3.5-turbo to the much larger GPT-4o was smaller, with diminishing returns beyond 100B parameters; the comparison is qualitative and model scale is not isolated from inference context. Rows r2, r3, r4, and r5.
